adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:165 — Delete still requires rulerRule, which the list view no longer provides, so Delete disappears from the list even when prom abilities grant it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly updates AlertRuleMenu to support permissions from either the ruler rule OR the Grafana Prom rule. It now computes `canDelete` as `(deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)` after calling `useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, ...)` (now accepts `RulerRuleDTO | undefined`) and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(promRule ? promRule : skipToken, ...)`. This means Delete does not “still require rulerRule”; it can be granted purely via prom-rule abilities when the list view only has `promRule`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:124 — Pause still requires a Grafana rulerRule, so Pause disappears from the list view even though canPause is computed from the prom rule.

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the diff explicitly adds Grafana Prom rule ability checks via useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...) and computes canPause as an OR of rulerPauseAbility and grafanaPauseAbility: `const canPause = (pauseSupported && pauseAllowed) || (grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed);`. The finding claims Pause still requires a Grafana rulerRule and would disappear in list view, but nothing in the shown diff supports that; the new logic is specifically intended to allow Pause based on promRule abilities even when rulerRule is absent/skipToken is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:87 — Abilities are OR-ed across ruler and prom checks, so a permissive prom result (for example, missing provenance or ruler still loading) overrides a restrictive ruler verdict such as provisioned/immutable, which re-enables Delete/Pause/Export on the detail page.

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the final permissions are computed by OR-ing ruler-based and GrafanaPromRule-based abilities (e.g. `canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`). In useAbilities.ts, the GrafanaPromRule path determines immutability/provisioning via `isProvisionedPromRule(rule)` which depends on `promRule.provenance` (added as an optional field in GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase). If `provenance` is missing/undefined on the prom rule, `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` will treat the rule as mutable and can return supported+allowed based on folder RBAC, even if the ruler rule would mark it immutable/provisioned and return NotSupported. Because AlertRuleMenu ORs the two results instead of preferring the restrictive one, a permissive prom result can re-enable actions like Delete/Pause/Export when the ruler verdict would disable them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:296 — Immutability now depends only on the optional prom `provenance` field; if the Prometheus API omits it, provisioned rules silently show as editable/deletable.

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, immutability is determined via `isProvisionedPromRule(rule)` which is `Boolean(promRule.provenance)` (see `utils/rules.ts`), and `provenance` was added as an *optional* field on `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` (`provenance?: string`). If the Prometheus/Grafana Prom rules response does not include `provenance` (or it’s unset for some provisioned rules), the code will treat the rule as non-provisioned and allow edit/delete based on folder permissions. The diff alone doesn’t prove the API can omit this field for provisioned rules, but the new logic does rely on that optional field for immutability.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:325 — Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently/Export are now gated on isAlertingRule instead of any Grafana-managed rule, which silently removes these actions for Grafana recording rules.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a behavior change in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`: `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore`, and `DeletePermanently` are now supported only when `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` (and not for `grafana.recordingRule`). In the previous logic (now applied in `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`), these actions were gated by `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` which would have been true for both Grafana alerting and recording rules. This could remove menu/actions for Grafana recording rules, but whether that is a defect vs. intended tightening of supported actions isn't provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx:68 — Dropping the ruler query removes the Creating/Deleting operation states, so rules created but not yet in prom are invisible and deleted rules keep showing working actions until prom catches up.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly removes the Ruler-side query and the reconciliation logic in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx`: `useGetGrafanaRulerGroupQuery` is deleted, `matchRules`/`promOnlyRules` are deleted, and the UI no longer renders `GrafanaRuleListItem` with `operation={RuleOperation.Creating}` for ruler-only rules nor `RuleOperationListItem` with `operation={RuleOperation.Deleting}` for prom-only rules. So the finding’s observation about losing Creating/Deleting operation states is grounded. However, whether this is an actual correctness defect depends on whether prom vs ruler can still be temporarily inconsistent (the removed code even commented that prom rules “should be strongly consistent now”), which cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:40 — The rule view href no longer carries returnTo, so navigating back from a rule loses the list's filter/scroll context.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `returnTo` query param from Grafana-managed rule links. Previously, `GrafanaRuleListItem` (in the deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`) built `href` via `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new `public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` sets `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo`, so any back-navigation mechanism relying on that param to restore list context would no longer work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rules/RulesTable.test.tsx:60 — Tests mock both ability hooks wholesale and never assert the Delete/Pause/Silence menu items actually work with a prom-only rule, so the regressions above pass CI.

adjudication.rationale: In `RulesTable.test.tsx`, the PR expands mocking to cover new hooks (`useRulerRuleAbilities`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, etc.) and sets default implementations that just return `[false,false]` for each action. The tests shown only drive/verify top-level action buttons (e.g., Edit/Delete) and do not exercise `AlertRuleMenu`’s new combined logic (OR-ing ruler abilities with Grafana Prom abilities) for menu actions like Pause/Silence/Export, nor do they cover the “prom-only”/skipToken pathway introduced in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` and `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` (using `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/Abilities` when only `promRule` exists). This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap around newly added nontrivial permission logic, not a directly verifiable runtime bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:124 — canPause is now granted from promRule but MenuItemPauseRule still requires rulerRule, so Pause never appears in the list view where rulerRule is undefined

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:263 — Prom-based abilities use isAlertingRule where ruler version used grafana.rule (alerting+recording), so Export/Pause/Restore/DeletePermanently become unsupported for Grafana recording rules

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` the diff changes support checks for several actions to depend on `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` (see `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, `Restore`, `DeletePermanently`). For Grafana Prom recording rules, `isAlertingRule` will be false, so these actions become unsupported. The older ruler-based logic (`useAllRulerRuleAbilities`) used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` (Grafana-managed alerting+recording) for these actions, so this is a concrete behavior change. The diff doesn’t prove this is incorrect (tests/comments suggest some actions are intended only for alerting rules), but it’s a specific edge-case/behavioral change worth confirming.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:82 — OR-combining ruler and prom abilities lets the prom path (which assumes AlwaysSupported and ignores ruler availability/loading) override a NotSupported ruler verdict when both rules are passed, e.g. rule viewer

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `AlertRuleMenu` now OR-combines abilities from the ruler path and the Grafana Prom path (e.g. `canPause = (pauseSupported && pauseAllowed) || (grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed)`), and the new Grafana Prom abilities come from `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, which sets `MaybeSupported` to `AlwaysSupported` (when not `loading`) and does not factor in `isRulerAvailable`. So, when both `rulerRule` and a Grafana `promRule` are provided (as in the rule viewer), the Grafana Prom path can make an action appear supported even if the ruler-based ability is `NotSupported` due to ruler availability/loading. However, the diff alone does not show that this leads to a broken action or incorrect authorization enforcement (it may be intended to allow list-view behavior without ruler API calls), so it’s a concrete design/edge-case concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:227 — Provisioned/immutable detection now depends on new optional `provenance` field on prom rules; if the Prometheus API omits it, provisioned rules become editable/deletable in the list

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `isProvisionedPromRule(promRule)` which treats a Grafana Prom rule as provisioned only when `Boolean(promRule.provenance)` is true, and `provenance` is added as an *optional* field on `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` (`provenance?: string`). In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `immutableRule` depends on `isProvisionedPromRule(rule)`, and immutability gates Update/Delete/Pause/Restore support. Therefore, if the Prometheus API response omits `provenance` (or doesn’t populate it for provisioned rules), provisioned rules would be treated as mutable in the list view. The diff alone doesn’t prove the API will omit it, but it does show the logic is now fragile because it relies on an optional field for immutability enforcement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:572 — Rule view href no longer includes returnTo, so navigating back from the rule detail page loses the list view filter/location

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previous `returnTo` propagation when building the rule view link for Grafana-managed rules. Deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx` used `const returnTo = createReturnTo();` and `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`, while the new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` sets `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` with no `returnTo` param. This is a concrete behavior regression: navigating to the rule view from the list will no longer encode the list location/filter for returning. (The cited line number is wrong, but the issue is present in the new file.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:56 — Parallel ruler and prom ability hooks with five hand-written `(a && b) \|\| (c && d)` merges duplicate logic that belongs in one combined helper/hook.

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the diff introduces two parallel multi-ability hooks (useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities) and then manually merges each action’s supported/allowed pair into canPause/canDelete/canDuplicate/canSilence/canExport via repeated `(supported && allowed) || (grafanaSupported && grafanaAllowed)` blocks. This is real, diff-grounded duplicated logic that would be cleaner/less error-prone as a shared helper or combined hook, but it does not constitute a verifiable functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:290 — useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities copy-pastes most of useAllRulerRuleAbilities' ability map instead of sharing a builder, so the two will drift.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new hook `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities()` that builds its own `abilities` map in a `useMemo` (around the newly added section starting with `export function useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...)`). This map is structurally very similar to the existing `useAllRulerRuleAbilities()` map just above (same `AlertRuleAction.*` keys and similar support/immutability logic), but it is duplicated rather than shared via a common builder/helper. This is a concrete maintainability/architecture concern grounded in the diff: future changes to ability semantics would need to be made in two places and could drift.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:346 — useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable reimplements useIsRuleEditable's folder-permission logic (even flagged "// duplicate" inline) instead of reusing it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable()` inside `useAbilities.ts`, with an inline comment `// duplicate`, and it reimplements folder-based permission checks via `useFolder(folderUID)` and `ctx.hasPermissionInMetadata(...)` using `getRulesPermissions('grafana')`. This is clearly duplicated logic similar in intent to `useIsRuleEditable(...)` (which also computes edit/remove based on rule source + permissions), and the reviewer’s point is a maintainability/architecture concern rather than a correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:244 — Refactoring useAllAlertRuleAbilities to delegate drops the isFederatedRuleGroup check and leaves a commented-out TODO, which silently regresses federated immutability.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` and no longer passes/derives the `CombinedRule.group` needed for federated detection. Inside `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, the prior federated logic is explicitly removed and replaced with `const isFederated = false;` plus a TODO comment (`// TODO: Add support for federated rules`). Previously federated status contributed to `immutableRule` (disabling edit/delete). With `isFederated` hardcoded false, federated rules would no longer be treated as immutable, which is a behavior regression introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:380 — A custom module-local `skipToken` Symbol duplicates RTK Query's skipToken concept and leaks into callers, which is confusing when both are imported.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces and exports `export const skipToken = Symbol('ability-skip-token');` in `useAbilities.ts`, and callers now import and use it (e.g., `AlertRuleMenu.tsx` and `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx`) to conditionally disable Grafana Prom rule ability checks. This does create a new exported token named `skipToken` that mimics the “skip token” pattern and leaks into consumer code. While the diff does not show RTK Query’s `skipToken` being imported in the same modules, the naming/API overlap and exported token are real and could be confusing in a codebase that also uses RTK Query’s `skipToken`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:51 — Component calls both useRulerRuleAbility and useGrafanaPromRuleAbility on every render and ORs them, so callers can't tell which data source is authoritative.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows RuleActionsButtons.V2 calling both hooks on every render: `useRulerRuleAbility(rule, groupIdentifier, AlertRuleAction.Update)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken, AlertRuleAction.Update)`, then computing `canEditRule` by OR-ing the two results. This is a real, diff-grounded design/authority concern (permissions can come from either path without making the source explicit), but the diff alone doesn’t prove incorrect behavior—comments indicate this dual-check is intentional for list-view vs ruler-backed contexts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:51 — Redundant `rule && rule.type === PromRuleType.Alerting` check and `rule?.` optional chaining on a required, already type-narrowed prop.

adjudication.rationale: In GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx the prop `rule` is required (`rule: GrafanaPromRuleDTO`), so `rule && ...` and `rule?.health`/`rule?.lastError`/`rule?.isPaused` are indeed redundant, but this is only a minor style/cleanup nit and does not represent a defect or meaningful review issue grounded in the diff’s behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:386 — useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities are parallel copies of the ruler single/multi wrappers, adding a second exported API surface to maintain.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new exported ability API for GrafanaPromRuleDTO: `skipToken`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`, and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` in `useAbilities.ts`. These are structurally parallel to existing ruler wrappers (`useRulerRuleAbility` / `useRulerRuleAbilities`) and effectively duplicate the single/multi wrapper pattern for a second rule type. This increases the public hook surface and ongoing maintenance burden without being a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/locales/en-US/grafana.json:3895 — Unrelated i18n churn (removing ad/irm/synthetic/cloud-feature-badge keys and adding a trailing space to "Cloud & Enterprise ") is mixed into this alerting change.

adjudication.rationale: In the shown diff for public/locales/en-US/grafana.json, the only i18n change is removing two alerting rule-list strings: "cannot-find-rule-details-for" and "cannot-load-rule-details-for". There is no evidence of removing ad/irm/synthetic/cloud-feature-badge keys or adding a trailing space to "Cloud & Enterprise ". The finding references changes that are not present in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:83 — OR-combining ruler and prom abilities lets a permissive prom-rule result override a ruler-side denial (e.g. provisioned/immutable), exposing pause/delete/export actions that should be hidden.

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the PR changes permission gating from a single source to an OR of two independent ability computations: e.g. `canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)` (same for Pause/Duplicate/Silence/Export). This can make the UI show actions whenever either hook is permissive. Since `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` explicitly blocks immutable/provisioned/plugin-provided rules (`immutableRule` => `MaybeSupportedUnlessImmutable` => NotSupported), but `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` determines immutability from `isProvisionedPromRule(rule)` which relies on optional `promRule.provenance` (added as `provenance?: string`), a missing/undefined provenance on the prom DTO would make the prom-side abilities treat the rule as mutable and thus enable actions. The OR-combination would then expose pause/delete/export/etc despite a ruler-side denial.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:61 — Edit ability is granted if either ruler or prom check passes, so a ruler-side immutability denial can be bypassed by the prom-rule path.

adjudication.rationale: In RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx the Edit gate is `canEditRule = (editRuleSupported && editRuleAllowed) || (grafanaEditRuleSupported && grafanaEditRuleAllowed)`. This means the UI will show Edit if *either* the ruler-based check or the GrafanaPromRule-based check allows it, even when the other path denies it. Since the two ability computations are implemented differently (e.g., useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities uses `AlwaysSupported` vs ruler abilities depending on ruler availability/other rule-derived conditions), this creates a concrete risk of inconsistent authorization/immutability handling when both `rule` and `promRule` are present. The finding’s specific claim about “ruler-side immutability denial” being bypassed isn’t fully provable from the diff alone, but the OR-combination issue is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:296 — Provisioned detection for prom rules relies on an optional `provenance` field; if the Prometheus API omits it, provisioned rules show as editable/deletable (fails open).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `provenance?: string` on `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` (optional) and then uses it as the sole signal for provisioned-ness in `isProvisionedPromRule()` (`Boolean(promRule.provenance)`), which feeds into immutability logic in `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities()` (provisioned rules become non-editable/deletable). If `provenance` is absent/undefined at runtime, the UI will treat the rule as non-provisioned and allow edit/delete actions. However, the diff alone does not prove the Prometheus API ever omits this field, so the “fails open” scenario is a robustness/compat concern rather than a verifiable defect from the change alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:203 — Test asserts exactly 4 menu items despite granting delete/update perms, locking in the regression where Pause and Delete vanish because AlertRuleMenu still gates them on rulerRule

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows AlertRuleMenu was refactored to *not* gate abilities solely on `rulerRule`: it now computes abilities from both `useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, ...)` (with `rulerRule` allowed to be `undefined`) and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(promRule or skipToken, ...)`, and then ORs them for Pause/Delete/Duplicate/Silence/Export (e.g., `canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`). So the claim that Pause/Delete vanish “because AlertRuleMenu still gates them on rulerRule” misreads the change. While GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx does assert there are exactly 4 menu items, the diff does not establish that Delete/Pause should be present in that menu nor that this assertion encodes a regression caused by ruler-only gating.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:187 — Silence menu item is only asserted present, never clicked; with promRule-only the SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer requires rulerRule so the action is a silent no-op that no test catches

adjudication.rationale: The updated GrafanaGroupLoader now renders list items solely from Prometheus rules (promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules) and no longer fetches/passes any rulerRule. In GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx, the new test only asserts the Silence menu item is present after opening the menu, but never clicks it or asserts any resulting behavior. Given the refactor to promRule-only rendering, this is a concrete coverage gap for the Silence action’s behavior in this new mode. However, the claim that SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer specifically requires a rulerRule and becomes a silent no-op cannot be verified from the diff shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:468 — New useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities/useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable (provisioned, plugin-provided, recording-rule, folder loading/missing, skipToken) have no direct unit tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new logic in `useAbilities.ts`, including `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, the internal `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`, `skipToken`, and the `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/Abilities` wrappers. The PR updates/creates component tests (e.g., `RulesTable.test.tsx`, `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`) that may exercise some paths indirectly, but the diff shows no new unit tests targeting these hooks directly (no `useAbilities.test.ts` additions or similar). Given the new edge-case handling (folder missing/loading, provisioned/plugin-provided rules, silence support, skipToken behavior), the absence of direct hook-level tests is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rules/RulesTable.test.tsx:199 — RulesTable tests fully mock useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities/useRulerRuleAbilities, so they check mock wiring and not the real OR-combination of ruler and prom abilities

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the new OR-combination logic lives in components (e.g., AlertRuleMenu combines results from useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities). In RulesTable.test.tsx the hooks are mocked, but that does not inherently prevent testing the component’s OR logic—mocking only bypasses the hooks’ internal implementations. The finding’s claim that mocking means the tests "check mock wiring and not the real OR-combination" is not verifiable from the diff and is based on an incorrect premise (the OR-combination is not inside the mocked hooks).

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rules/RulesTable.test.tsx:218 — useGrafanaPromRuleAbility is mocked but the singular hook is not used by the rendered RulesTable path, so that setup is dead and misleading

adjudication.rationale: In `RulesTable.test.tsx` the default `beforeEach` sets up `mocks.useGrafanaPromRuleAbility.mockReturnValue([false, false])`, and one Grafana test further mocks `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`. But the diff shows the two relevant rendered components/hooks are: `AlertRuleMenu` now uses `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (plural) and `useRulerRuleAbilities` (plural), while the test’s own comment states `RuleActionsButtons` uses `useAlertRuleAbility` (singular). Nothing in the shown diff indicates the `RulesTable` render path calls `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` (singular), so that mock setup is likely dead/misleading test scaffolding rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:139 — New promRule-only paths (getEditableIdentifier returning null for non-Grafana promRule, getIsProvisioned via isProvisionedPromRule hiding Edit) have no tests

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new promRule-only logic paths in RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx: getEditableIdentifier() now returns undefined (and the component returns null) when no ruler `rule` is provided and `promRule` is not a Grafana prom rule (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule)`), and getIsProvisioned() now checks `isProvisionedPromRule(promRule)` when only `promRule` is present. The updated/added tests exercise Grafana prom rules (e.g., GrafanaGroupLoader and RulesTable RBAC mocking Grafana prom abilities), but the diff shows no tests that cover (a) passing a non-Grafana promRule to RuleActionsButtons (ensuring it returns null / logs warning) or (b) the provisioned/promRule provenance path affecting behavior. This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a demonstrable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:82 — Tests for Creating/Deleting operation states and matchRules were deleted with no replacement coverage for ruler/prom inconsistency behavior now dropped

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `matchRules` and the dual Ruler/Prom fetching in `GrafanaGroupLoader.tsx` (Ruler query + Creating/Deleting operation rendering + warning log are all deleted), and `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` correspondingly deletes the tests that covered the “only ruler rule exists (Creating)” / “only prom rule exists (Deleting)” states and all `matchRules` unit tests. New tests cover menu/button rendering, but there is no longer any test coverage (or code) for ruler/prom inconsistency handling after the refactor. This is a concrete, diff-grounded reduction in edge-case handling/coverage; whether intended or acceptable is a design decision, not a direct defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/FilterView.tsx:157 — FilterView switched from GrafanaRuleLoader to GrafanaRuleListItem (no loading/error/not-found handling, showLocation) without any test of the filter view rendering

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows FilterView.tsx switching from <GrafanaRuleLoader .../> to <GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} ... showLocation={true} /> (public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/FilterView.tsx). GrafanaRuleLoader (now deleted) previously encapsulated its own loading/error/not-found states and performed queries; GrafanaRuleListItem is a pure renderer that assumes a fully-populated GrafanaPromRuleDTO and does not provide those states. Whether that is correct depends on upstream data guarantees, which are not verifiable from this diff alone, but the finding’s point that this is an important behavioral change in FilterView with no accompanying FilterView-focused test coverage is diff-grounded and actionable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:160 — Missing-permission test only checks Edit is hidden and More exists; it does not verify menu actions are restricted or cover a provisioned prom rule

adjudication.rationale: In GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx the new RBAC test “should not render edit button when user lacks edit permissions” only asserts Edit is absent and More is present; it never opens the menu nor asserts that menu items (Silence/Duplicate/Export/Delete) are restricted when permissions are denied. This is relevant because the diff adds new nontrivial permission/ability logic for Grafana Prom rules (AlertRuleMenu now ORs ruler vs GrafanaProm abilities via useRulerRuleAbilities/useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, and useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities introduces folder-permission-based edit/delete + provisioned/immutable handling via isProvisionedPromRule/provenance). There’s also no test covering provisioned prom rules (provenance) affecting immutability/available actions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:115 — More-button test only asserts aria-label/text content, a low-value check that doesn't exercise any permission logic

adjudication.rationale: In GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx, the new test `should render More button with action menu options` indeed only checks presence plus `aria-label`/text for the More button, but the diff also adds separate tests that do exercise permission-driven rendering (`should not render edit button when user lacks edit permissions`) and menu action availability (`should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked`). So calling this out as a review “finding” about missing permission logic coverage is misleading; it’s at most a minor/low-value test nit, not a substantive diff-grounded issue.
